text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Capped Wallaby and Easts powerhouse second-rower John Welborn won the annual Norwich Rising Star award in Sydney last night, beating several New South Wales rugby union season success stories to join the ranks of past winners including Sam Payne and Danny Manu. Page 25.

Australian Rugby Union officials have had enough of the English Rugby Football Union's stonewalling and internal bickering, giving the dysfunctional heads of rugby an ultimatum in regard to the proposed on-again/off-again test against England to formulat a "grand slam" tour. Page 24.

North Sydney Bears could become embroiled in a legal battle with Penrith over winger Scott Pethybridge who was signed secretly for next season by Norths development and recruitment staff. At this stage very little is being disclosed. Page 26.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Rugby league referee coordinator Mick Stone predicts a low penalty count and some fast and furious football between the final four for the deciders of who will play in the rugby league grand final. Page 50.

Croatia is gambling on a slow clay court for the Davis Cup tie against Australia to boost their chances in the doubles, while counting upon Goran Ivanisevic to win singles against Mark Philippoussis and Jason Stoltenberg. Page 51.

Former Australian test and limited overs cricket legend Denis Lillee has turned down an offer by English county side Lancashire to become their head coach because of ACB coaching commitments, forcing the luckless Lancs to revise strategies. Page 51.
THE AGE

Greg Matthews is poised to make the most remarkable comeback of Test cricket. After three and a half years the all-rounder, who incidentally turns 37 in December, could be called upon for the coming tour of India to replace injured leg-spinner Shane Warne Page B8.

The saviour of the Melbourne Demons, mining tycoon Joe Gutnick, was last night crowned king as he accepted the presidency of the club. It was also passed last night that a 75 percent majority of members would be needed to initiate any future merger options. Page B8.

Essendon believes Sydney Swans full-forward Tony Lockett will not play in Saturday night's preliminary final, despite Swans coach Rodney Eade ruling him in the side. Plugger yesterday admitted to the media his groin was not 100 percent right as yet. Page B8.
HERALD SUN

Fitzroy football players accused of a drunken rampage on an end of season Bali trip face tough action from the club and the AFL. The footballers are claimed to have destroyed rooms, abused other resort guests and spat on staff. Page 1.

Geelong's anticipated purge of players has begun with half-forward Shayne Breuer being offered as part of a pre-draft trade to Port Adelaide. Although other players have remained silent about possible moves, Ablett, Couch and Brownless will remain with the Cats next year. Page 94.

West Coast forward Peter Sumich was banned for one match for striking Essendon's Gavin Wanganeen in last Saturday's AFL semi-final at the Cricket Ground. The suspension will be served during the opening round of the Ansett Cup next season. Page 94.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

North Sydney Bears coach Peter Louis has appealed to the referee in Saturday's sudden-death clash with St George to stop the Saints from controversial play, such as interfering with the Bears players in attack. Page 104.

The Kelaher Brothers demolished the Oxford University Tourists in humiliating fashion, in a game which stereotyped the difference between the speed and aggression of southern hemisphere rugby and set-piece northern play. Sydney University, static in AAMI, was convincing against Oxford 38-5. Page 94.

Wallaby prop Dan Crowley is afraid he will miss the coming Australian tour of Europe after having a bone in his toe amputated this week, keeping him immobile for at least three weeks. Wallaby medico John Blest said the injury will not prevent the prop from flying out with the team. Page 94.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
